'''Thomas W. Baumgarte''' (born 1966) is a German physicist specializing in the [[numerical relativity|numerical simulation]] of [[compact objects]] in [[general relativity]].

==Career==
Baumgarte completed his BSc in 1992 at [[LMU Munich]] and his PhD in 1995 also at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=http://www.bowdoin.edu/~tbaumgar/cv.pdf|title=Thomas W. Baumgarte : Curriculum Vitae|website=Bowdoin.edu|accessdate=6 July 2018}}</ref> He worked as a postdoc at [[Cornell]] University and [[University of Illinois]] and is currently a professor of physics at [[Bowdoin College]].  He is the author of over 65 articles about general relativity and astrophysics (for example, [[black holes]], [[neutron stars]], and [[gravitational collapse]]). In 2010, along with [[Stuart L. Shapiro]], he published a book on numerical relativity. In 2012, he received the Bessel Prize.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uni-jena.de/Mitteilungen/PM121103_Baumgarte.html |title=Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena // Kollisionen Schwarzer Löcher |access-date=2018-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322001752/http://www.uni-jena.de/Mitteilungen/PM121103_Baumgarte.html |archive-date=2014-03-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Baumgarte is married to Karen Topp, who is also a professor at Bowdoin College.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bowdoin.edu/profiles/faculty/ktopp/index.html|title=Karen A. Topp {{!}} Bowdoin College|website=www.bowdoin.edu|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref>
